sentences.text: The Southern Taurids come from a broad dust stream shed over centuries by Encke, the comet with the shortest known period.
Encke circles the Sun in only three point three years; it is now in the outer half of its orbit.
Earth takes weeks to pass through this wide stream; the particles enter the atmosphere relatively slowly, at twenty-eight kilometres a second.
That is why the Taurids produce few but long-lasting meteors, often as bright as fireballs.
The radiant lies in Taurus; this year the late moonrise keeps the sky dark until midnight.
